full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Quddus, J. :- This Rule, at the instance of a judgment debtor in a money decree, was issued calling in question order dated 5.4.2010 passed by Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka in Artha Execution Case No.131 of 2009 rejecting the petitioner's application filed under Order XXI rule 83 of the Code of Civil Procedure for permission to sell an attached property through private negotiation for enhancement of the sale proceeds. 

 2. The facts leading to this writ petition are that respondent No.3, United Commercial Bank Limited, Bangshal Branch, Dhaka as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No.33 of 2003 before the Artha Rin. Adalat No.3, Dhaka against the defaulting borrower M/S Florida International and others for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 1,80,92,680.24 (One crore eighty lac ninety two thousand six hundred eighty and paisa twenty four) only. In the said suit the petitioner company, as a third party mortgager, was made defendant No.3. Ultimately the suit was decreed exparte against the borrower and on contest against the petitioner by judgment and decree dated 25.5.2009. The decree holder bank put the decree in execution by filing Artha Execution Case No.131 of 2009 and initiated selling of schedule-A property out of 4 (four) schedules. The petitioner company is the owner-in-possession of the said property, which it mortgaged in favour of the decree-holder bank as a third party mortgager. The schedule-A property costs at Taka 50,00,00,000/- (fifty crore), while the execution case was filed for 'realization of Taka 2,76,36,732.66 (Two crore seventy six lac thirty six thousand seven hundred thirty two and paisa sixty six) only. 

 3. At one stage the petitioner filed an application under Order XXI Rule 83 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (briefly 'the Ain') in the said execution case stating inter alia, that the prevailing market price of schedule-A property was much higher than the entire outstanding dues as claimed by the decree-holder bank. Though the petitioner-company was a third party mortgagor, it was willing to pay the entire outstanding dues by adjustment from the sale proceeds, if it would be allowed to sell schedule-A property through private negotiation and enhance the sale proceeds. The petitioner further stated that due to incurring loss in business, it was not in a position to pay the decreetal amount with interest thereon in cash. 

 6. The decree-holder bank as respondent No.3 appears and contests the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition without specifically controverting the material facts as stated in the writ petition and submits that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain is a special law and the provision of the Code of Civil Procedure is not applicable in a suit/ proceedings under the Ain and that the executing Court has not committed any illegality in rejecting the petitioner's application. 

 7. Mr. Shah Md. Monir Sharif, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner supports the rule submitting that section 26 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 provides that the Code of Civil Procedure, so far it is not in consistent with the Ain, would he applicable in an execution proceedings. In the present case if the petitioner-company is r allowed to sell schedule-A property by private negotiation, it will not affect the interest of the decree-holder bank in any manner, but the petitioner will be benefited. 

 "83. (1) Where an order for the sale of immovable property has been made, if the judgment debtor can satisfy the Court that there is reason to believe that the amount of the decree may be raised by the mortgage or lease or private sale of such property, or some part thereof, or of any other immovable property of the judgment-debtor, the Court may, on his application, postpone the sale of the property comprised in order for sale on such terms and for such period as it thinks proper, to enable him to raise the amount. 

 Provided that all monies payable under such mortgage, lease or sale shall be paid, not to the judgment-debtor, but, save in so far as a decree-holder is entitled to set-off such money under the provisions of rule 72, into Court; 

 3. Nothing in this Rule shall be deemed to apply to a sale of property directed to be sold in execution of a decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage of or charge on, such property." 

 10. It appears from the ordering portion of the judgment as well as the drawn up decree .(vide annexure B and B-1 to the writ petition) that the concerned Artha Rin Adalat passed a simple money decree as follows : 

 We have further examined that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 specially the provisions regarding execution under chapter VI of the Ain and found that Order XXI rule 83 of the Civil Procedure Code does not conflict with any of the provisions' of the Ain. Therefore, we do not find any difficulty to hold that Order XXI rule 83 of the Civil Procedure Code will be applicable in an execution proceeding under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Sub-rule (3) of rule 83 under Order XXI as quoted above excludes mortgage decree from application of sub-rule (1) and (2) of the said Order, but since the decree before us is a simply money decree, Order XXI rule 83 (1)(2) of the Code would be applicable here.
